identification.summary: CeranaKeeper is a China-aligned APT group that ESET named in October 2024 [S1][S2]. ESET says it has been active since at least early 2022 and mainly targets government institutions in Southeast Asia, with Thailand the primary focus [S2][S4]. The name is wordplay on 'beekeeper' and Apis cerana (the Asian honeybee), based on a recurring string in the group's tools [S2]. It uses custom backdoors and abuses cloud and file-sharing services such as Dropbox, OneDrive, GitHub and PixelDrain for command and control and exfiltration [S2][S6].
identification.firstObserved: ESET: active since at least early 2022; campaigns against Thai government institutions observed from 2023 [S2][S4]. ESET white paper published 2024-10-02 [S6].
identification.notes: ESET separates CeranaKeeper from Mustang Panda: some of its activity was earlier attributed to Mustang Panda, but ESET concluded it operates independently, while possibly sharing information or third-party resources with it [S2][S4]. In Feb 2025 Trend Micro published on 'Earth Preta' activity using a TONESHELL variant; ESET said it tracks that threat as CeranaKeeper [S8][S9]. Trend Micro and ESET names are not interchangeable without the primary reports; see gaps.

attribution.confidence: ESET describes CeranaKeeper as 'China-aligned' [S2]. The sources gathered do not name a specific Chinese government agency or contractor.
attribution.basis: ESET assessment of tooling and targeting; the group shares some tooling or resources with Mustang Panda but ESET tracks it as a separate cluster [S2][S4].

objectives: Large-scale data theft from government institutions. ESET reported extensive wildcard expressions that sometimes traversed entire drives, which it said showed an aim of massive data siphoning [S4].

regions: Myanmar, Philippines, Japan, Taiwan (listed in one ESET press release; Thailand is the only country confirmed in ESET's own campaign findings) [S2]
targeting.notes: Sector and regional focus from ESET press materials and press coverage [S2][S3][S4]. Initial access routes were reported as unknown [S4].

capabilities.summary: Custom backdoors including TONESHELL, DropboxFlop (Python backdoor using Dropbox C2, apparently based on the public Dropflop project), OneDoor (C/C++ backdoor abusing OneDrive) and BingoShell (uses GitHub pull requests as covert C2, named for the string 'bingo#') [S2][S3][S4]. In a mid-2023 intrusion a compromised machine brute-forced a domain controller in a Thai government network, giving privileged access; the group then deployed TONESHELL and a credential-dumping tool and abused a legitimate Avast driver to disable security protections [S2]. Archived files were exfiltrated via cloud services, with a newer version using PixelDrain [S6]. In 2025 a TONESHELL variant was reported sideloaded through a legitimate Electronic Arts application and using MAVInject.exe to inject into waitfor.exe when ESET software was present [S7][S9].

campaigns.name: Earliest activity
campaigns.summary: ESET says the group has been active since at least early 2022.

campaigns.name: Thai government domain-controller intrusion
campaigns.summary: A compromised machine brute-forced a domain controller in a Thai government institution's LAN; the group gained privileged access, deployed TONESHELL and a credential dumper, and abused an Avast driver to disable protections.

campaigns.name: Thai government data theft campaigns
campaigns.summary: ESET observed several targeted campaigns against Thai government institutions in which large amounts of data were exfiltrated using Dropbox, OneDrive, GitHub and PixelDrain.

campaigns.name: ESET public disclosure
campaigns.summary: ESET published its CeranaKeeper research on 2024-10-02 and separated the group from Mustang Panda.

campaigns.name: Trend Micro 'Earth Preta' report and ESET response
campaigns.summary: Trend Micro reported a TONESHELL variant using MAVInject.exe when ESET software was present; ESET disputed that this was a bypass, said it updated its engine in January, and said it tracks the actor as CeranaKeeper.

diamond.adversary: China-aligned APT tracked by ESET as CeranaKeeper, distinct from Mustang Panda per ESET [S2][S4].
diamond.capability: TONESHELL, DropboxFlop, OneDoor, BingoShell; LAN brute force; credential dumping; driver abuse; cloud-service exfiltration [S2][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Legitimate cloud and code-hosting services (Dropbox, OneDrive, GitHub, PixelDrain) used for C2 and exfiltration [S2][S6].
diamond.victim: Government institutions, mainly in Thailand, with other Asian countries listed in one press release [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection of government data in Southeast Asia consistent with a China-aligned espionage mission, per ESET's 'China-aligned' characterization [S2][S4].
diamond.technology: Windows domain environments with weak credential controls and tolerance for outbound traffic to mainstream cloud services [S2].

gaps: I could not open the ESET WeLiveSecurity article, ESET white paper, or press releases directly (fetch failed); details come from search-result summaries of those documents and secondary coverage [S1][S2][S6]. Validate against the white paper.
Initial access vector is reported as unknown [S4].
No government attribution or named sponsoring agency found.
Overlap with Mustang Panda, Earth Preta (Trend Micro) and Stately Taurus (Palo Alto) is not resolved; Trend Micro and ESET cluster boundaries differ and should not be merged [S2][S8][S9].
Listed non-Thai victim countries (Myanmar, Philippines, Japan, Taiwan) rest on one press release and were not independently confirmed [S2].
Press sources disagree on which file-sharing services were used (Pastebin appears in one secondary source only); not included here.
No MITRE ATT&CK group ID known for this record.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is Windows domain controllers and file servers in government networks, plus outbound paths to cloud and code-hosting services [S2]. STEP 2: The actor blends C2 and exfiltration into Dropbox, OneDrive, GitHub and PixelDrain traffic and abuses signed drivers to disable security tools, which degrades detection built on network reputation [S2][S6]. STEP 3: Observed template is a foothold, LAN brute force against a domain controller, privileged access, TONESHELL and credential dumping, then wildcard sweeps and cloud exfiltration [S2][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued bulk collection from Southeast Asian government networks. MDCOA is use of the same cloud-abuse tradecraft against coalition or partner-nation government networks in a regional crisis. Candidate indicators: repeated failed logons against domain controllers from internal hosts, loading of an unexpected Avast driver, unusual GitHub pull requests containing 'bingo#', and bulk archive uploads to PixelDrain, Dropbox or OneDrive from servers [S2][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track partner-nation government networks in Southeast Asia as likely collection targets and share vendor indicators with partners. (2) Authorities: monitoring cloud-service egress on DoD networks and blocking driver loads need clear owners and approvals before an incident. (3) Mission assurance: protect domain controllers and mission file shares through credential hygiene and lockout alerting. (4) Coordination: because cluster boundaries (CeranaKeeper vs. Mustang Panda or Earth Preta) are unsettled, coordinate through DC3 and partner CERTs on indicators rather than waiting for name resolution [S2][S8].

provenance.importedSummary: CeranaKeeper is a China-aligned APT that has been active since at least early 2022, primarily targeting governmental institutions in Asian countries. The group employs custom backdoors like TONESHELL and OneDoor, leveraging cloud services such as Dropbox and OneDrive for data exfiltration. CeranaKeeper utilizes techniques like side-loading, brute-force attacks, and the deployment of BAT scripts to extend its reach within compromised networks. Their operations are characterized by a relentless pursuit of sensitive data, adapting their toolset and methods to evade detection.
